text_citations.passage: The actuator has a multiple-part outer housing 14 and an energy storage device 16 flanged or, more generally, fasseparate, externally closed assembly unit.

text_only.answer:
Part 16 is the energy storage device. It holds the return energy that drives the part 12 into a set end position if the drive fails. It appears in Figs. 1, 2 and 3, but I couldn't cite any drawing label spots because no OCR label list was provided for the sheets.

What it is: It is mounted on the actuator's outer housing 14 as a separate, externally closed assembly unit. Inside, a gear wheel 62 meshes with two opposing gear racks 64, and each rack has a pair of compression springs (66, 68 or 70, 72) that store the return energy. It connects to the second output shaft 38 through a hub, called coupling point 60. It pushes in only one direction; turning it over by 180° reverses that direction. When the drives fail, the holding devices release and the stored energy is let out all at once.

Where it is shown: Fig. 1 is the perspective view; the text says coupling point 60 "is also shown in FIG. 1". Fig. 2 is a schematic of part of the actuator together with the energy storage device. Fig. 3 is a cut-away view of the energy storage device. The description of Figs. 5–9 also mentions part 16, but those figures show the rotary entrainment device.

Inside, a gear wheel 62 meshes with two gear racks 64, which load pairs of compression springs (66, 68 and 70, 72). text_citations.quote: pin 48
text_citations.passage: US 11,976,746B2 7 Specifically, on the gear wheel 36, a pin 46 and a pin 48 are introduced into corresponding axial openings.

text_only.answer:
Part 48 is a pin on the second gear wheel 36, alongside pin 46. The two pins sit in axial openings in the gear wheel and are spaced the same distance from the central axis of the output shafts. They form the stop surfaces of the mechanical rotary entrainment device 40, which can couple the coaxial output shafts 34 and 38 so they turn together.

What it does: pin 48 works against pin 50, which is fixed to the first gear wheel 32.
- While the energy storage device is being charged, the driven pin 50 pushes pin 48 anticlockwise, so gear wheel 32 carries gear wheel 36 and the second output shaft 38 with it.
- If the drives fail, gear wheel 36 turns clockwise, and pin 48 pushes pin 50. This turns the first output shaft 34 and moves the part 12 to its first end position.

Where it is shown: the description places it in FIG. 4 (the rotary entrainment device 40 as a whole), FIG. 5 (pin 48 drawn in broken lines at the first end position and also in its moved position) and FIG. 6 (pin 48 at the second end position).

I can't point to label spots on the drawings because no OCR drawing labels were provided for this patent.

full.answer:
Part 48 is a pin on the second gear wheel 36. It is one of the stop surfaces of the mechanical rotary entrainment device 40 that links the second output shaft 38 to the first output shaft 34.

- Mounting: pin 48 is fitted into an axial opening in gear wheel 36, alongside a second pin, 46.
- Function: the pins act as stop surfaces that let the two coaxial output shafts be coupled in the direction of rotation.
- Position: pins 46 and 48 sit on the same circle around the shared central axis of output shafts 34 and 38.
- Mating pin: pin 50 on the first gear wheel 32 is on the same circle and comes into contact with pins 46 and 48.
- Loading the energy storage device: when the first drive turns, pin 50 pushes pin 48 anticlockwise. This carries the second output shaft along and tensions the springs.
- Fail-safe return: if the drives fail, the released energy storage device turns gear wheel 36 clockwise. Pin 48 then pushes pin 50, which drives the first output shaft 34 and moves the part to its first end position.

Where it is shown (label 48):
- FIG. 4 (sheet 5): D5-7
- FIGS. 5 and 6 (sheet 6): D6-2 and D6-10
- FIGS. 7 and 8 (sheet 7): D7-3 and D7-10
- FIG. 9 (sheet 8): D8-5

Pin 48 is also drawn with broken lines in FIG. 5 to show the starting position, when the energy storage device is almost empty.

text_only.answer: Part 60 is the multispectral filtering chip, also called the multispectral imaging chip. It is the core of the chip-based multispectral camera (the primary camera 52). It is made up of a photosensor 62 covered by an array (matrix) of narrow bandpass filters 64. These filters pass only a few target wavebands of incident light 66 (for example about 420-440, 520-540 and 690-710 nm) and block all other light. The chip works with active illumination and software so the device can detect contamination whatever the ambient light. It is shown in FIG. 3, a color schematic elevation view of the chip, which is also cited as the best view of the filter matrix. No drawing-label data was provided, so I can't point to a specific label spot for part 60.

Part 35 is the primary transfer line exchanger in the cooling section. I can't point to where it appears on the drawings, because no drawing labels were provided with this patent.

What it is: The reference list names 35 as the "Primary transfer line exchanger." In FIG. 1 (cracking furnace system 40), the feedstock/dilution steam mixture 13 is heated in the first high temperature coil 23 and then in the primary transfer line exchanger 35.

Part 52 is the second bonding layer, which is part of the third connecting piece 50.
